findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public IP and exposing the MySQL endpoint to the internet, which greatly expands the attack surface for credential brute-forcing and exploitation.
storage_encrypted = false means the RDS volumes and snapshots are stored unencrypted, so anyone with access to the underlying storage or a copied snapshot can read the data.
The master username is the predictable 'admin' and the password comes from var.password which is passed in plaintext to Terraform state and to EC2 user data; no IAM auth or Secrets Manager is used.

The user_data script embeds the database username and the plaintext master password into the instance metadata. Anyone able to reach the instance metadata service (including via SSRF from the PHP app) can retrieve the DB credentials.

The role attached to the web instance grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", allowing full control of all S3 buckets, EC2, and RDS in the account if the instance or the PHP app is compromised.

No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled and an SSRF in the hosted PHP application can steal the instance role credentials (which carry wildcard S3/EC2/RDS permissions).
No root_block_device/ebs encryption configuration is specified, so the instance volume holding the database credential include file may be stored unencrypted.
The database security group allows all outbound protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised database host.

The security group has no description and relies on rules defined elsewhere; combined with the public accessibility of the DB instance, the VPC-wide ingress rule effectively permits any resource in the VPC to reach MySQL rather than only the app tier.
Port 3306 is open to the entire VPC CIDR instead of being restricted to the application security group, so any compromised host in the VPC can attempt to authenticate to the database.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced for DB connections
findings.description: The MySQL parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = ON, so the publicly reachable database accepts unencrypted client connections and credentials/data can be intercepted in transit.
The database endpoint of a publicly accessible instance is emitted as an unmarked Terraform output, disclosing the target host to anyone with access to state or CI logs.
